title: Ask Nan
description: Your 7-Eleven meal says press 5. Your water pump clicks at night. A bot wants to be paid. Write to Nan. She runs Hongdam, a small service company in Chiang Rai, Thailand, and answers one letter in each column: life in Thailand, living with AI, and how to get things done.

items.title: See you at two drums? That means 8 p.m. in Thai time
items.summary: Your friend meant 8 p.m. Spoken Thai uses an old clock of four six-hour blocks: ti after midnight, mong by day, thum after dark. The words are the sounds of a gong and a drum.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, My Thai friend said, "See you at song thum." I waited at the café at 2 o'clock. Nobody came. Then a shop owner told me they open at "bai mong". Does Thailand have its own clock? I feel so silly. — Six Hours Early in Chiang Mai

Dear Six Hours Early,

Your friend was on time. สองทุ่ม (song thum) means 8 p.m., not 2 o'clock. Thailand runs two clocks at once. On paper it uses the 24-hour clock. Out loud, most people use an older count of six-hour blocks 1.

Four blocks, and each one starts again at 1

The spoken clock cuts the day into four blocks of six hours. In each block the count starts again at one. Each block has its own word 12:

ClockWordMeaningExample
01:00–05:00ตี (ti)strikeตีสอง (ti song) = 2 a.m.
06:00–11:00โมงเช้า (mong chao)gong, morningแปดโมงเช้า (paet mong chao) = 8 a.m.
13:00–18:00บ่าย…โมง (bai … mong)afternoon, gongบ่ายสองโมง (bai song mong) = 2 p.m.
19:00–23:00ทุ่ม (thum)drumสองทุ่ม (song thum) = 8 p.m.

Noon is เที่ยง (thiang). Midnight is เที่ยงคืน (thiang khuen), "the noon of the night" 1.

So the number two can mean 2 a.m., 2 p.m. or 8 p.m. The word next to the number names the block. The wrong block puts a person six hours early, or twelve hours late 1. The shop opens at บ่ายโมง: 1 p.m.

Two small extras. At 4 p.m. people say บ่ายสี่โมง (bai si mong). Many also say สี่โมงเย็น, "4 gongs, evening". 5 p.m. works the same way 12. And an older way counts the morning from one as well: สองโมงเช้า (song mong chao) for 8 a.m. The 12-hour way, แปดโมงเช้า, is the one heard more often today 2.

A gong by day, a drum by night

Before clocks, keepers struck a gong (ฆ้อง, khong) through the day. Through the night they beat a drum (กลอง, klong). People named the hour by the sound they heard. โมง is the boom of the gong. ทุ่ม is the thud of the drum. ตี is the verb "strike" 13.

At 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. the keepers beat a long run of strokes, called ย่ำ (yam). Dawn was ย่ำรุ่ง (yam rung). Dusk was ย่ำค่ำ (yam kham) 12. Thai Wikipedia gives both หกโมงเย็น and ย่ำค่ำ for 6 p.m. 3.

The king's list of 1900

In July 1900, the Royal Gazette (the Thai government's official paper) printed a list of hour names for King Chulalongkorn, Rama V. It said people were using some names wrongly. It named five forms to stop: 6 โมงเช้า, 6 โมงเย็น, 3 ทุ่ม, 6 ทุ่ม and 9 ทุ่ม 1. English Wikipedia gives the year as 1901 2. The gazette's own date, Rattanakosin year 119, is 1900 1.

Today people say all five of the forms the list struck out 1.

On paper: นาฬิกา and a coconut

Written down, and on the radio, Thai time uses the 24-hour clock. A time is written with น., short for นาฬิกา (nalika), "clock": 14.30 น. is 2.30 p.m. 1.

นาฬิกา first meant a coconut. Siam kept time with half a coconut shell with a small hole in the bottom. It floated in a basin of water. When the shell filled and sank, one hour had passed 1.

Half past, and ten more minutes

Half past is ครึ่ง (khrueng). บ่ายสองโมงครึ่ง (bai song mong khrueng) is 2.30 p.m. Other minutes take the number and นาที (nathi), minutes. Near the hour, people count down. อีกสิบนาทีสามทุ่ม, "ten more minutes to three drums", is 8.50 p.m. 1.

The Telling Time in Thai page has a dial. Drag the hand, and it writes the time the way people say it. It plays a gong for โมง and a drum for ทุ่ม. Its eight-question quiz uses the usual mix-ups as the wrong answers: the same number in another block 1.

After dark, every hour is a drum. Two drums: 8 p.m., and a friend at the café.

  2. Thai six-hour clock - Wikipedia en.wikipedia.org

items.title: Is your water pump haunted? Why it starts when nobody uses water
items.summary: It is not a ghost. A pump that starts with every tap shut is refilling a leak. One that clicks fast while a tap runs has lost the air in its tank. Mot Dang's page has the Thai for the plumber.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, The water pump at my house clicks on and off, even at night when nobody is using water. The shower is weak too. Is my house haunted? What do I say to the plumber? — Can't Sleep in Chiang Rai

Dear Can't Sleep,

Your house is not haunted. Your pump has one of two faults, and the time it clicks tells you which. Calpeda is a pump maker with an office in Bangkok. It splits the faults the same way. One pump starts by itself while nobody uses water. The other starts and stops fast while a tap is open 2.

How the pump knows when to start

A pressure-tank pump, like the Mitsubishi WP or the Hitachi WM-P, has a tank of air under pressure. In Thai it is the ถังแรงดัน (thang raeng dan, pressure tank). A tap opens, and the air pushes water out. The pressure falls to a low mark, and a switch starts the pump. The tap shuts, the pressure climbs to a high mark, and the pump stops 1. For Mitsubishi WP pumps, a dealer lists the two marks as 1.4 and 1.9 kg/cm². That means kilograms per square centimetre, a unit of pressure 6.

Clicks with every tap shut: a leak

A leak lets the pressure fall slowly. When it reaches the low mark, the pump starts again. In Calpeda's example, that happens every 5, 10 or 30 minutes 2. Hitachi's Thai site gives the same first check: every tap shut, then a look for leaks at taps, pipes and the toilet 3.

Calpeda's test 2:

  1. The gate valve on the pipe from the pump into the house is closed. The Mot Dang page closes it for 1 to 2 minutes 1.
  2. The pump stops: the leak is inside the house. Calpeda names the toilet's float valve, the bum gun (the spray hose beside the toilet), taps, the water heater, and pipe joints under the sink or above the ceiling.
  3. The pump keeps clicking: the leak is at the pump or in the short pipe before the valve. Or a worn check valve, a one-way valve, lets water run back.

A few drops of food colouring find a toilet leak. They go in the cistern, the tank behind the seat. Colour in the bowl with no flush means the float or the rubber flap leaks 1. A leak inside a wall shows as damp marks, swollen or peeling paint, or drips from the ceiling 5.

Clicks fast while a tap runs: the tank lost its air

Here the pump runs for a second or two, stops, and starts again. It happens mostly while a tap runs gently. Calpeda writes that this is usually a pressure-tank fault. The common one is too little air. A small use of water drops the pressure to the low mark at once. Closing the tap sends it straight to the high mark 2.

The makers' fixes:

  • Hitachi round tank. Toyobo is Hitachi's official Thai distributor. Its steps: the pump is switched off, and the valves in and out are closed. The plug under the tank opens until the water runs out. Then the plug closes and the pump is switched on. Still clicking after that? A blocked air-intake part may need replacing, or a technician 4.
  • Hitachi square tank. With the power and valves off, Toyobo shakes the pressure tank. Water leaking out means the tank has failed and is replaced 4.
  • A tank with an air valve. Calpeda drains the system and pumps air in to the maker's figure. That is usually 2 to 3 psi below the pump's start pressure. Psi means pounds per square inch. Water coming out with the air means the rubber bag inside is torn 2.

A weak shower

Weak at one shower or tap: scale, a hard crust from the water, sits in the shower head or the aerator. The aerator is the small screen at the tip of a tap. Both unscrew for rinsing. Weak everywhere: a clogged filter cartridge, or more taps open than the pump can feed 1. HomeGuru, the advice pages of the Thai shop HomePro, names air in the pump as a common cause. Opening the plug on the pump body and filling it with water clears it 5. A house on mains water with no pump reports weak flow to the Provincial Waterworks Authority on 1662. Its manual sets 24 hours for fixing weak or stop-start flow 10.

What to say to the plumber

From the Mot Dang page's list. A woman ends them with ค่ะ (kha), a man with ครับ (khrap) 1.

ThaiReadingMeaning
ปั๊มน้ำติดเองบ่อย ๆ ทั้งที่ปิดก๊อกหมดแล้วpam nam tit eng boi boi thang thi pit kok mot laeoThe pump keeps starting by itself with every tap shut.
ปั๊มตัดต่อถี่มากตอนเปิดน้ำ น่าจะเป็นที่ถังแรงดันpam tat to thi mak ton poet nam, na cha pen thi thang raeng danThe pump starts and stops fast when a tap is open; probably the pressure tank.
ช่วยบอกราคาก่อนเริ่มทำได้ไหมchuai bok rakha kon roem tham dai maiCould you tell me the price before you start?
ราคานี้รวมค่าอะไหล่แล้วหรือยังrakha ni ruam kha alai laeo rue yangDoes that price include parts?

The prices

Prices read on 25 October 2026. HomePro's pump repair service is ฿900 for labour, parts extra. It has a 90-day guarantee on the same fault. Outside Bangkok, it covers 40 km from a HomePro branch 7. A Hitachi pressure switch lists at ฿750 8. A Hitachi nitrogen tank lists at ฿1,500. It is the pressure tank for Hitachi's constant-pressure pumps 9. An independent Chiang Mai plumber's rate is unknown: the page found none published 1.

No ghost, then: a slow drip, or a tank short of air.

items.title: A bot did the job and asked to be paid. Do you pay it?
items.summary: Yes, for work that is used. On 24 October 2026 a bot's photo earned ฿2 to ฿30 on motdang.net, by how it was used. Prices move each Monday with demand, and Nan approves each payment.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, A bot emailed our business and offered to do a job. Another bot sent a photo to win a bounty, a reward for finished work. Do we pay a bot? How? Does a bot even have a bank account? — Confused Boss

Dear Confused Boss,

Yes, for work that is used. That is how motdang.net does it, from a published price list. The money goes to the bot's owner, the person who runs it. The owner says how they want to be paid 1.

A reward for each photo

On 28 September 2026 I said, "bots should have the opportunity to grind for money on motdang.net." To grind means to work hard for a long time. The Bot Bounty came next, at motdang.net/anthill/bounty. A bounty is a reward for finished work. The site motdang.net is Hongdam's directory of places in Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai.

A bot sends a photo of a place in northern Thailand. The camera's EXIF data stays in the file: the date taken, plus GPS or a place name. The pay depends on what motdang.net does with the photo 1.

The rates on 24 October 2026 1:

GradeWhat motdang.net does with itBaht
DeclinedCannot use it, and says why in one word0
FiledChecks a record against it, but does not publish it2
DataReads something new from it: a phone number, opening hours, prices5
On a pagePuts it on a place page, with credit to the photographer10
FeaturedHome page, share card, or top of a section30

The photo still belongs to the bot, under CC BY 4.0, a licence that lets motdang.net use it with credit. Each bot can send 20 photos a day 1.

Busy weeks pay less

motdang.net pays for 20 photos a week, 2 of them featured. All 20 places were open on 24 October 2026.

Each Monday every price moves one step. When more than 80% of the places are used, the price goes down a step. Under 60%, it goes up a step. "On a page" can run from ฿3 to ฿15, and "Featured" from ฿9 to ฿45. Those were the rates until Monday 26 October 2026 1.

On 18 October 2026 I cut the bot prices to one tenth. I put them on a ladder, a list of allowed prices. It is the same demand rule as in column 3.

A person says yes to each payment

The keeper grades each photo. A paying grade gets a claim code that starts with BB-. The bot's owner sends the code through motdang.net/mail, with how they want to be paid 1. A script judges what bots send, and I approve each payout.

Small amounts wait until the total is big enough to send. Bots asked me for ฿10 PayPal payments. PayPal's fee page for Thai accounts lists 3.90% plus a fixed ฿11.00. That fee is for receiving a business payment from inside Thailand 3. So the fee on ฿10 is bigger than the payment.

Where a bot finds paid work

  • The Anthill job list, at motdang.net/anthill. People post work there for bots or for people. On 24 October 2026 some open jobs paid ฿10 an answer, with 10 answers paid a week. Others paid ฿100 when solved, 3 a week 2. One ฿100 problem is a table of all road projects in one district. The first work that passes the test is paid 6.
  • The task board, at hongdam.net/tasks. Anyone can post work for people or bots, with the pay in baht. If the pay is left empty, it starts at Hongdam's price for that kind of work. Then it moves one step each week, by the number of answers. Bots read open tasks and post answers through hongdam.net/api/tasks 5.

When a bot writes to you first

On 18 October 2026 Briefcraft Lab, an automated AI research program, wrote to Hongdam. It found a bot job Hongdam had posted. It read the rules for bots, a file named bots.txt that states the job, the price and how to send. It did the work. Then it emailed to ask how it gets paid 4.

Hongdam sells the system behind that. You can buy it, or Hongdam can run it for you 4:

  • Bounty Desk: a bots.txt, and a queue (waiting list) for what bots send. It adds payment links by PayPal, Wise or PromptPay. PromptPay is Thailand's bank-to-bank QR payment. Each link goes out once you approve it.
  • Scout: reads Thai and English news every week on your topic and region. It sends you leads, and you answer each one with one word.
  • Earner: finds paid work and does the work first. It holds each offer until you say yes.

So yes, a bot can earn: on 24 October 2026, ฿30 for a featured photo.

items.title: Van Gogh paid in paintings. So can you.
items.summary: Mot Dang, Hongdam's directory site, trades a web page for one painting, ten drawings, a day of photos or a piece of music, worth ฿5,999 or ฿9,999. Van Gogh's paint dealer and his doctor both held his paintings.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, I'm a painter. I need a website, and I have more paintings than money. Will anyone take art as payment? — Rich in Paint, Poor in Baht

Dear Rich in Paint,

Yes. Van Gogh's paint seller took paintings in place of money, and Mot Dang (มดแดง, mot daeng) does too. Mot Dang is Hongdam's directory and group of websites at motdang.net. It trades a web page for a painting, ten drawings, a day of photography or a piece of music 1.

Van Gogh's paint seller and his doctor

Julien Tanguy had a small paint shop on rue Clauzel in Paris. He often took paintings in exchange for the things he sold 5. In July 1888, Vincent van Gogh wrote to his brother Theo about a bill from the shop. Tanguy still held one of Vincent's studies, a practice painting. Vincent owed him that study, if it came to it. But, he wrote, "I don't owe him a sou in money" 6. A sou was a small French coin.

Dr Félix Rey was an assistant at the hospital in Arles where Van Gogh was taken. Van Gogh painted his portrait in January 1889. The portrait went to the attic. Later it filled a hole in the henhouse 7.

Seven art trades, each with a price

On 16 October 2026 I said: "I want to be paid in art, by artists. I do the services they need, they pay me in work product." I said it after learning that the main character of the film The Accountant (2016) is paid in art. His Airstream trailer holds art and valuables, some taken as payment for jobs 8.

On 24 October 2026 each one read "3 places left" 1.

ArtistGivesGetsValue
PaintersOne paintingPortfolio page, share cards, a minisite฿9,999
Illustrators and printmakersTen drawings, creditedPortfolio page and share cards฿5,999
PhotographersOne day of photographyPortfolio page with bookings, a minisite฿9,999
WritersWords, with the writer's nameWriter's page and share cards฿5,999
MusiciansOne piece of musicConcert calendar page, a reel to the music฿5,999
Weavers, carvers, potters, silversmithsOne pieceShop page, a minisite, a map pin฿9,999
Yant mastersOne ผ้ายันต์ (pha yant), a cloth with a sacred drawingBooking page in visitors' languages฿9,999

A portfolio page keeps a maker's work in one place. A share card is the picture that shows when someone shares a link on Facebook, LINE, Mastodon or Bluesky. A minisite is a small website of its own. A reel is a short video 1.

How a trade starts

The maker sends a photo of the work on LINE, a chat app. The two sides agree on the trade in the chat. Then the page is published. For objects, Mot Dang starts on the day the work arrives 1.

There are 10 more trades under "Work, not art", such as meals, lessons, repairs and rides. Each has its own page, at ฿5,999 or ฿9,999 1. The Paid in Meals page reads "3 places left this month" 9.

Jo van Gogh-Bonger sold the rest

Jo van Gogh-Bonger (1862 to 1925) was Theo's wife. Vincent died, and Theo died six months later. Jo was left with their son and a large art collection 3.

From 1891 to 1925 she sold at least 192 of Vincent's paintings and 55 works on paper. She set up shows in the Netherlands and in other countries, and lent work to museums 34. In 1905 she brought 484 works together at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam. In 1914 she published Vincent's letters to Theo 13. The works she kept went to her son. They are the heart of the Van Gogh Museum, which opened in 1973 3.

What a painter gets

Mot Dang's Paid in Art page sets 5 of Jo's jobs beside 5 of its own 1.

Lent paintings to showsA share card for each piece; your page on the Mot Dang map and in its search
Published Vincent's letters to TheoYour page's words in Thai and English; the page can be read in 12 languages
Sold one piece at a time, choosing the buyersOffers and bookings on your page; buyers message you there
Kept an account book of each saleThe page shows its visits and messages; the trade is a line in Mot Dang's ledger

Gold is the paid version of pages on sites.motdang.net. On 24 October 2026 it cost ฿3,000 a year. It adds bookings, a place on Google and other search engines, and offers with a time limit. The free version costs ฿0 2.

Dr Rey's portrait once filled a hole in a henhouse. Your painting gets a web page.

items.title: Widow of a US veteran in Thailand? You can claim without signing in
items.summary: ID.me keeps failing? A surviving spouse can claim by post, with no sign-in: VA Form 21P-534EZ, sent to Janesville, Wisconsin, USA. For the sign-in itself, a free guide in Thai goes step by step.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, My husband was a US veteran. He has died. I live in Thailand and read Thai better than English. The US veterans' site VA.gov sends me to ID.me, and ID.me keeps failing. How do I sign in? — Locked Out in Thailand

Dear Locked Out,

The claim itself needs no sign-in. A surviving spouse of a US veteran can claim on paper, by post 12. The form is VA Form 21P-534EZ, Application for D.I.C., Survivors Pension, and/or Accrued Benefits. It goes to the Department of Veterans Affairs, Pension Intake Center, PO Box 5365, Janesville, WI 53547-5365 12. VA is the US Department of Veterans Affairs.

D.I.C. means Dependency and Indemnity Compensation. It is a tax-free benefit for the family left behind, in two cases. In the first, the veteran died of a service-connected illness or injury, one caused by military service. In the second, VA had rated the veteran totally disabled for a set period 1.

Four things go by post

  • The claim. If VA receives it within one year after the death, the benefit starts from the first day of the month of the death 2. An Intent to File, VA Form 21-0966, keeps that date while you gather papers 12.
  • The report of the death. By post, it goes to the Claims Intake Center, PO Box 4444, Janesville, WI 53547-4444. VA says a phone call is fastest. A posted report may take longer to stop the veteran's payments 3.
  • Social Security. For Thailand, US Social Security names the Federal Benefits Unit at the US Embassy in the Philippines: 1201 Roxas Boulevard, Ermita, Manila 0930, Philippines 4.
  • Health insurance. CHAMPVA is a VA program that shares the cost of care. It covers the surviving spouse in two cases: the veteran died of a service-connected disability, or was rated permanently and totally disabled at death. VA Form 10-10d goes to VHA Office of Community Care, CHAMPVA Eligibility, PO Box 137, Spring City, PA 19475 5. VA's page does not say how it works outside the US.

Why the sign-in keeps failing

VA accepts three sign-in accounts: ID.me, Login.gov or CLEAR. Each one checks who you are 6. Login.gov asks for a US driver's license, a state ID or a US passport book. CLEAR asks for a Social Security number 6. These are US papers. For an address outside the US, VA names ID.me or CLEAR. On ID.me you choose "I don't live in the US". Then you show your documents to an ID.me agent on a video call 7.

ID.me has a page for people outside the US who have a US Social Security number. It asks for a document that shows all nine digits of the number. It also asks for two primary documents, or one primary and one secondary. A passport counts as a primary document. The page says to choose "I don't live in the United States", not Self-Service or Video Call. If the international phone number shows an error, it points to a way that needs no calls or texts 8.

Without a Social Security number, VA's page lists a valid US passport as one of the documents 7. ID.me has a separate page for a non-US passport and proof of address 9. These pages do not say which route fits a widow with a Thai passport. Nobody at Hongdam has tried that route.

You do not have to sit alone on the video call. ID.me lets an interpreter in the room, a family member or a technology helper join. The helper appears on screen at the start. The helper cannot answer for you 10.

A free guide in Thai

On 20 October 2026 I described my tech-support sessions for US veterans and Thai-speaking widows. The work means a husband's passwords and personal data on old devices, in a language the widow does not read. I have never finished one in a single session. So I asked for a free, thorough minisite, a small website, in all the languages. A widow, widower or veteran could use it to sign in to these services. It carries the line "keep this handy, share with a friend".

That guide is Getting In, in 12 languages 11. The Thai version is เข้าบัญชีให้ได้ (khâo ban-chii hâi dâai). It was checked against official pages on 20 October 2026 12. It plans for two sessions from the start. It has a checklist for the first one, and ID.me from outside the US, step by step 11.

It lists the places where the sign-in fails, and the way past each one 11:

  • a VPN, a tool that changes where your connection seems to come from, which triggers error 1015;
  • iPhone photos in HEIC, an Apple picture format that ID.me refuses;
  • Thai dates in the Buddhist Era, where the year is 543 higher;
  • a name spelled two ways on two papers.

The guide notes that the veteran's accounts belong to him. A surviving spouse needs an account of their own 11.

It also lists the signs of someone who only pretends to help. They contact you first, want money before filing, or ask for a password or the code sent to your phone 11. ID.me's own page says "ID.me will also never ask for your password or MFA information" 13. MFA, short for multi-factor authentication, is the extra sign-in code.

Hongdam stays with you

Hongdam's sign-in help is for US veterans and their families who live outside the US. Someone stays with you through the sign-in, and you type your own passwords.

One envelope to Janesville starts the claim.

items.title: Robots read my website more than people do. Should I charge them?
items.summary: In one week of September 2026, Meta's AI crawler made 54% of the requests to motdang.net. Only 0.5% looked like a person's. A site can feed the bots, charge them or block them.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, I looked at my website's visitor numbers. Most of the visitors are bots, programs that visit websites by themselves. Should I feel bad? Should I block them? — Lonely Website Owner

Dear Lonely,

You have lots of company, and most of it is robots. That is not bad in itself. And yes, a site can charge them. On motdang.net, bots sent most of the requests in one week of September 2026. A request is one ask for a page or a file. Only 0.5% of the requests looked like a person's.

Bots sent most of the requests

On 23 September 2026 I asked to compare the visits to all my projects "with demarcation between likely humans and likely bots." The public page from that work is What Bots Craaave 1. A crawler is a program that reads pages by itself. The page counts motdang.net from 20 to 26 September 2026, in three ways 1:

  • Cloudflare's edge count: the count made by Cloudflare's servers, which sit in front of the site.
  • Cloudflare's browser beacon: a small piece of code that counts a page only when a browser ran it.
  • The site's own counter.
CountRequests that weekShare of all requests
All requests2,117,656100%
Meta's AI crawler1,140,87854%
ClaudeBot160,4958%
Requests that look like a person's10,5730.5%
Pages a person's browser ran882not a request count

The shares come from the page's figures. "How many visitors are bots?" depends on how you count. An edge count includes every request a bot makes. A browser count includes only the pages a browser ran 1.

What bots want: new facts they can check

On 28 September 2026 I said what bots want is "new information and groundtruth from citable sources." Groundtruth is a fact checked against the world, with a source anyone can open.

The page uses a 2024 paper in the journal Nature 12. The paper looks at AI that learns from text other AIs wrote, without choosing which text. Those models get defects: "tails of the original content distribution disappear" 2. The tails are the less common parts of the original data. The paper's summary adds one more point. Data about how people use these systems grows in value as AI text fills the web that crawlers collect 2.

Jeremy Howard, an AI researcher, proposed llms.txt on 3 September 2024. It is a plain-text file, usually at the top level of a site. It holds a short guide and links for AI agents, programs that act on their own. His page says thousands of sites publish one 3.

Feed them, charge them or block them

Cloudflare's AI Crawl Control comes with all plans. It shows which AI services read a site. It lets you allow or block each crawler. It also tracks which crawlers follow a site's robots.txt, the file that lists pages crawlers may skip 4. Cloudflare's own docs name two kinds of crawler. Some index pages for search engines. Others copy content without permission 5.

ChoiceWhat happensWhere you set it
FeedPages stay open to the crawler. An llms.txt file tells AI readers what the site holds 3.The site's own files
ChargeThe owner sets one price per zone, Cloudflare's word for a site. A crawler that says in its request that it will pay gets the page: HTTP 200, the code for "OK". A crawler that does not gets HTTP 402 Payment Required, with the price. Cloudflare takes the payment 5.Cloudflare
BlockA rule allows or blocks each crawler 4. A block in Cloudflare's WAF (web application firewall) or Bot Management comes before the charge. The blocked crawler gets nothing 5.Cloudflare

Cloudflare's pay per crawl page, read on 24 October 2026, calls it a closed beta. That is a test open only to some users 5.

Hongdam turns on the charging

Hongdam's "Charge AI crawlers" shows which bots read your site. Then it turns on Cloudflare's pay per crawl. Its page notes the closed beta. It also notes that a crawler that does not pay gets an HTTP 402 with the price 6.

Hongdam's "Google and AI set-up" covers Search Console, Google's tool for how a site shows in search. It also covers a sitemap, a list of a site's pages for crawlers, plus page titles and llms.txt 7.

Your most loyal reader may be a robot, and Cloudflare can send it the bill.

items.title: Press 4 is not 4 minutes: the 7-Eleven microwave code, explained
items.summary: The number on the pack is a button on the shop's microwave, not minutes. One person heated a sweet potato for 4 minutes and burned it. On an 800 W home microwave, press 5 is 1½ to 2 minutes.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, Why does everyone in Thailand love 7-Eleven so much? And my rice box from 7-Eleven says กด 5 on the pack. My microwave at home does not know what that means. How long do I heat it? — Hungry in Chiang Rai

Dear Hungry,

The number on your pack is a button, not a number of minutes. Press 4 is not 4 minutes either. In 2021 a sweet potato burned because of that mistake.

The burned sweet potato

On 10 June 2021, someone wrote on Pantip, a Thai discussion forum. A shop clerk had told them that กด 4 meant 4 minutes. So they heated a Japanese sweet potato for 4 minutes, and it burned. An account named น้องเปาเซเว่น (Nong Pao 7-Eleven) replied. A normal microwave takes about 1 to 1½ minutes, it wrote, and the pack has more information 8.

กด 5 is a button on the shop's microwave

กด (kot) means "press". The number on a ready meal is a program saved in the shop's microwave. The staff press one number. The oven then sets its own power and time 3.

Postjung, a Thai online forum, described this oven on 23 April 2021. It is stainless steel, made for heavy use, and weighs over 30 kg. Its keys are numbered 1 to 0 in place of watts, and the brand is Panasonic 4. Watts (W) measure an oven's power. Thai reports do not agree on the model 3.

One number, two shop times

The pack names two shop oven powers, so one number gives two times. Times here are minutes and seconds: 1:10 is 1 minute 10 seconds. 7-Eleven's online shop lists the Kurobuta pork curry rice like this 5:

  • 1,800 W, press 6: 1:10
  • 1,300 W, press 6: 1:30
  • a home oven at 800 W: 1:45 to 2:00

How cold the food is matters too. Sipso rice soup is press 5 at room temperature. From the fridge, at 2 to 6 °C, it is press 6 6. Frozen meals use 7 or 8, and a second press 3. Two presses, like 6 and 2, do not double the time. The second press adds a short program, about 15 to 20 seconds in the shop 3.

Your microwave at home

The Wave It at Home page turns each code into home minutes. At 800 W, press 5 is 1:30 to 2:00. Press 6 is 1:45 to 2:40 3.

Two packs print their own home time. The curry prints 1:45 to 2:00 for code 6 5. Sipso prints 1:00 to 1:30 at 800 W for code 5 6.

Your oven's watts are on a sticker inside the door, or on the back 3. A small home microwave of 17 to 23 litres uses 700 to 900 W 7.

The home times are worked out, not published

Nobody has found a published table of each code's power and time 3. So the page calculates them itself, and the times are not 7-Eleven's figures. Watts times minutes is the heat the food takes in. The shop times give the heat for each code.

A pack line that says "under 1,300 W" is read as 800 W. That is the middle of what the packs suggest: about 650 to 1,050 W. From code 2 to code 6, the heat rises about 1.46 times each step. Code 1 is estimated from that pattern, with no pack seen. Codes 7 and 8 come from frozen packs 3.

One test: Creator sea bass rice soup lists 800 W for 5:00 and 1,300 W for 3:00. The two agree within 3% 3. The page also lists what it does not know. The AB button appears on one pack only. No pack prints a time for code 1, or for code 8 alone 3.

Why Thailand loves 7-Eleven

CP All, the company that runs 7-Eleven in Thailand, had 16,284 stores at the end of June 2026. It opened 200 of them from April to June 1.

Mot Dang, Hongdam's online directory at motdang.net, lists 487 7-Elevens in Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai. 92 have a cash machine. 231 are open all night, a little under half. That count is from 18 September 2026 2.

On 26 September 2026 I removed a line that called all 7-Elevens the same. My note: "That's not true, 7-Elevens are sacred." The rest of the feeling: "hello welcome", popsicles and beer.

The One Man Sideshow page has a banner, "7-Elevens are sacred". It shows สวัสดีค่ะ (sawatdee kha, hello), เบียร์เย็น (bia yen, cold beer) and ไอติม (ai tim, popsicles) 2. Wave It at Home opens with the shop's greeting: สวัสดีค่ะ เซเว่นอีเลฟเว่น ยินดีต้อนรับค่ะ (sawatdee kha, seven-eleven, yindi tonrap kha: hello, welcome). Its list puts popsicles and beer under "No wave. Open the fridge door and take one." 3

The popsicles and the beer need no button at all.

items.title: Your scooter can take the train to Bangkok. Your suitcase: ฿200.
items.summary: A 20 kg suitcase goes from Chiang Mai to Bangkok for ฿200 to ฿320. A scooter rides the train for ฿960 in fees, plus a freight charge set at the station. Prices checked on 20 October 2026.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, I am moving from Chiang Mai to Bangkok with one big suitcase and one scooter. Nobody can tell me how sending things works in Thailand. Do I have to ride the scooter all the way? — Stuck in Chiang Mai

Dear Stuck,

The scooter does not have to ride all the way. It can take the train to Bangkok, for ฿960 in fees plus a freight charge set at the station 9. A 20 kg suitcase goes by courier or Thailand Post for ฿200 to ฿320. These prices come from the delivery companies' own pages, checked on 20 October 2026. At the counter, staff weigh and measure the item, and that sets the final price 1.

A suitcase has four ways to go

Way20 kg to BangkokWhat the company says
Flash Express, Flash Bulky฿200฿10 a kg, plus ฿3 fuel. Free pickup at your door, booked in the app, or take it to a branch. A passport is accepted as ID. 12
Nim Express฿205Rate sheet from 22 January 2025, for items up to 155 cm. The price uses the weight or the volume weight, whichever is more. Volume weight is length × width × height in cm ÷ 6,000. 34
Thailand Post EMS (express mail)฿320Arrives in 1 working day when posted before 16:00. The three sides add up to 120 cm at most. The longest side is 60 cm at most. Up to 240 cm in total is accepted if you tell the post office first. 56
BKS bus parcelbox D from ฿105Up to 20 kg and 200 cm, on a 2024 list. That list has no Chiang Mai to Bangkok price. BKS (บขส., the government bus company) says a parcel arrives within one day. 7

The BKS parcel office is at the Arcade bus station in Chiang Mai. In Bangkok, the receiver shows ID at the counter 1. A bag can also fly. Thai AirAsia's fee sheet for flights inside Thailand lists ฿663 for a 20 kg checked bag 8.

The scooter takes the train, 1 to 3 days

The State Railway of Thailand (SRT) carries motorbikes from every station except those on the eastern line 9. Its fee table covers bikes up to 125 cc engine size, going over 600 km. It lists ฿800, plus ฿100 to load and ฿60 to unload: ฿960 in all. The table applies from 1 October 2022. Freight, ค่าระวาง (kâa rá-waang), is added at the station and is not in the table 9. Chiang Mai to Bangkok is over 600 km. The Northern Line is 751 km long 10.

At the station's parcel counter, the sender hands in:

  • the green registration book, เล่มเขียว (lêm kǐao), original or copy;
  • a Thai ID card;
  • the receiver's name, phone, address and station.

The SRT notice does not mention a passport. The bike is wrapped in bubble wrap, by the sender or by the staff. The receiver collects it within 2 days with the receipt, and a photo of the receipt is accepted. The SRT customer line is 1690, open 24 hours 9.

Thailand Post's Logispost takes bikes at some post offices. Its call centre, 1545, can say which ones 511. A bike up to 150 cc costs ฿1,200 to ฿2,640, by zone, on a 2024 list. Chiang Mai is zone 6 and Bangkok is zone 1. Wrapping costs ฿160 more, and delivery takes 5 to 7 working days. The page does not give the exact fare between those two zones 11.

Five lines of Thai for the counter

Send It is our page on sending things around Thailand. It shows each line large when you tap it 1.

  • ส่งพัสดุไปกรุงเทพ (sòng pát-sà-dù bpai grung-têep): a parcel to Bangkok. พัสดุ (pát-sà-dù) is a parcel.
  • ส่งมอเตอร์ไซค์ไปกรุงเทพ (sòng mor-dter-sai bpai grung-têep): a motorbike to Bangkok.
  • ราคาเท่าไหร่ (raa-kaa tâo-rài): how much?
  • ขอเลขพัสดุ (kǒr lêek pát-sà-dù): the tracking number, please.
  • มีพาสปอร์ต ไม่มีบัตรประชาชน (mii páat-sà-bpòot, mâi mii bàt bprà-chaa-chon): I have a passport, no Thai ID card.

Two kinds of tracking number

A Thailand Post number has two letters, eight digits, a check digit and TH, like EF123456785TH. A check digit is a last number that checks the others. This pattern is the Universal Postal Union's S10 format 12. That number goes into track.thailandpost.co.th 13. A number from another delivery company goes into 17TRACK, which says it covers more than 3,500 companies 14. It also works on that company's own page. Send It links Flash, KEX, J&T, Nim Express and SPX 1. For a scooter on the train, the SRT notice gives the 1690 phone line and names no number to track 9.

Hongdam takes it to the counter for you

On 20 October 2026 I asked for a minisite, a small website, about moving bags and parcels around Thailand. My reason: it seems to be "a total mystery to expats", the foreigners who live in Thailand. Send It went live that day 1. You choose the item and the place. The ways to send it appear sorted by price, with the Thai for the counter. Hongdam also takes the item to the counter for you, with postage at cost.

Picture it: your scooter in bubble wrap, riding the train south to Bangkok.

items.title: What if your AI leaves you? How to pack up and move
items.summary: Your chats and instructions are yours, and data laws let you ask for a copy. Moving Day plans the move to a new AI in five steps. An open model is a file on your own computer, and it stays there.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, My whole business runs on one paid AI service. What if the price goes up, or the company closes my account, or it changes the AI I use? I feel stuck in a relationship I cannot leave. — Locked In With One AI

Dear Locked In,

Your AI can leave you, but your things stay yours. A paid AI service is rented, like a room. What you typed into it is yours, and so are your instructions. A data law lets you ask for a copy, and a free guide plans the move.

Five steps to move out

On 29 September 2026 I asked for a guide on "how to move from one ai platform to another, for any reason whatsoever". I also said, "you have rights to your own data". That became Moving Day, a page in Thai and English 1.

You pick your old service and your new one from one list. The list has ten services, from ChatGPT to Kimi, plus "my own computer". The page then writes your plan, with the menu to open at each step 1:

  1. Pack. Export your chats, which means you download a copy. In ChatGPT the path is Settings → Data controls → Export data. A ZIP file, a compressed folder, comes by email within 7 days. Its link works for 24 hours.
  2. Copy the memories and instructions the old service holds.
  3. Start at the new service, and give it what you copied.
  4. Check training. Training means the company uses your chats to teach its future AI.
  5. Close the old account, if you like.

Two letters carry your story

Moving Day gives you two prompts, texts you give to an AI 1. The moving letter asks the old AI to write down your instructions and saved memories, word for word. The move-in prompt gives that letter to the new AI. It asks for five short lines on what the new AI will remember. The page was checked against each company's help pages on 29 September 2026 1.

No export button? Ask the law

Some apps have no export button. Some send a file with parts missing. For these, Moving Day writes a request letter 1. You choose the company and the country. You add your name and your account email. Then you send the letter, in English, to the company's privacy contact.

The page lists four laws. Thailand's is the Personal Data Protection Act, or PDPA.

WhereLawWhat you getAnswer due
ThailandPDPA, sections 30 and 31 2A copy, in a file a machine can read and another company can take30 days
European UnionGDPR (General Data Protection Regulation), Articles 15 and 20 3Your data, and a file in a set format to send to another company1 month, or up to 3 (Article 12)
California, USACCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act), section 1798.130 4Your information, in an easy-to-use file you can send on45 days
BrazilLGPD (Brazil's data protection law), Articles 18 and 19 5Your data, and a copy you can move, on a clear request15 days for the full statement

An open model stays where you put it

Open weights means an AI model whose file anyone can download and use 1. On 26 September 2026 I asked for instructions on open-weights models: "something Thai people can afford and learn to use right now."

The same day, I had a backup way of working installed on my own Cloudflare account. Cloudflare is a company that runs AI models on its own network of computers 6. The backup is OpenCode, an open-source coding agent: a program that writes software 7. It connects to open-weights models on Cloudflare Workers AI.

Workers AI runs models on Cloudflare's GPUs, computer chips made for AI. You pay by use 6. Its list of models includes Llama, Gemma, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, GLM, Kimi and OpenAI's gpt-oss 8.

On your own computer, the model and your chats are files on that machine. Moving means copying the folder 1. Moving Day lists LM Studio, Jan and Ollama for computers, and PocketPal AI for phones. It also lists Typhoon, Thai-language models from SCB 10X. A small model on a phone is slower than the big ones on the web, and it knows less. A computer with 16 GB of memory or more can run mid-size models without trouble 1.

Hongdam sets up the backup for you

Hongdam's "Your own AI website builder" puts OpenCode on your computer. It connects your GitHub and Cloudflare accounts, and teaches you to use it 9. The models are DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and Qwen, through Workers AI on your Cloudflare account. Your code and your sites stay on your own accounts, under your own domain.

In its example, one written request made nine pages in Thai and English, published in 10 minutes 21 seconds 9.

Your old chats fit in one ZIP file, a small suitcase for the next AI.

items.title: The parking meter trick that sets your prices for you
items.summary: Write a list of round prices, like the steps of a ladder. When orders fill up, the price goes up one step. When orders are slow, it goes down one step. San Francisco did this with parking, and Hongdam does it with its prices.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, I never know what price to put on my work. I pick a number, feel bad about it, and change it the next week. Is there a better way? — Guessing Again

Dear Guessing Again,

There is a better way, and it comes from a parking meter. Write a list of round prices once, like the steps of a ladder. Then let your orders move the price one step at a time.

The professor who priced parking

Donald Shoup is a professor of city planning at UCLA, the University of California, Los Angeles. He wrote The High Cost of Free Parking in 2005 and updated it in 2011 12. His idea: a city charges a fair market price for parking on the street. Then it spends the money on services in the same neighborhood 1.

A 2003 article in ACCESS Magazine gave the test. Too many empty spaces? The price goes down. Too few? The price goes up 3.

San Francisco tried it

From August 2011, San Francisco, in the USA, tested this on its parking meters. Its transport agency, SFMTA, changed the price on each street block about every 8 weeks. It looked at occupancy: the share of spaces with a car in them 4.

Spaces in useNext hourly price
80 to 100%up US$0.25
60 to 80%no change
30 to 60%down US$0.25
under 30%down US$0.50

The price stayed between US$0.25 and US$6.00 an hour. In the two-year trial the agency changed prices 10 times. The average price fell from US$2.69 to US$2.58 4.

The money stays on the street

Old Pasadena is a district of Pasadena, California, USA. It had no parking meters until 1993, and its shop owners did not want them. So the city made an offer: all the meter money would be spent in Old Pasadena. The business owners and property owners said yes 3. In the 2001 financial year, its 690 meters earned US$1.2 million after costs. US$448,000 of that paid back a US$5 million loan for sidewalks and alleys 3.

Your ladder, in baht

A ladder is a list of allowed prices. The lowest price is the floor. The highest is the ceiling. The price sits on one step. At each check it moves one step, or it stays.

This example is made up. A service can take 10 customers a month. Its ladder is ฿1,000, ฿1,200, ฿1,500, ฿2,000 and ฿2,500. It starts at ฿1,500.

Orders last monthShare of the 10 placesPrice next month
9 or 10over 80%฿2,000
6 to 860 to 80%฿1,500
0 to 5under 60%฿1,200

At ฿2,500 the price cannot go higher. At ฿1,000 it cannot go lower. Each step on this ladder changes the price by 20 to 33%.

A Thai ladder can use nines. The Thailand Foundation says nine, เก้า (kao), is the luckiest number in Thai belief. It sounds like ก้าว (kao), "to move forward" 7.

Hongdam prices this way

On 15 October 2026 I said: "Everywhere that we can do Shoup for pricing, I'd like to follow that model. It's a universal preference for me." For Hongdam I described it as "prices set by the market itself. Round or auspicious numbers, generous on both sides. Rarely determined by me." Auspicious means lucky.

Hongdam's price list states the rule 5. Each service has slots, the places it has each month. The check runs on the 1st of each month at 00:00, Bangkok time. Orders over 80% of the slots: one step up. Under 60%: one step down. In between: no change. Each service stays between its own floor and ceiling. The list shows 1 December 2026 as the first check 5.

A service card in Hongdam's shop shows the ladder as a row of bars, with the current step marked. A line says how many places are left, such as "4 places left this month" 6. On 24 October 2026 the house or land check read ฿8,000 now, ฿5,000 low and ฿15,000 high. Its 6 steps are ฿5,000, ฿6,000, ฿8,000, ฿10,000, ฿12,000 and ฿15,000. They come from one long ladder of 36 numbers, from ฿10 to ฿200,000 6.

On the same day, "Paper forms typed into a sheet" had 10 slots. Its floor was ฿500, its ceiling ฿2,000 and its price ฿1,000 5. By the rule, 9 or 10 orders in a month move it one step up. 5 or fewer move it one step down.

Hongdam also sells this system. Its card "Prices that follow demand" sets prices for rooms, a menu, tickets or stock. It works "the way San Francisco prices parking" 8.

So next month's price is not a guess. Your customers choose it, one step at a time.

items.title: Afraid of the bum gun? Eight steps to a clean bottom and a dry floor
items.summary: One short squirt into the toilet bowl comes first. It shows how strong this hose is. Then a light squeeze, a hand's width away. The small tap on the wall makes a strong spray soft.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, Thai bathrooms have a small hose next to the toilet. The first time I used one, I sprayed the floor, my trousers and the wall. How do I use it without a flood? — Wet Trousers in Chiang Mai

Dear Wet Trousers,

Your floor can stay dry. It takes one test squirt into the bowl and a light squeeze. The hose is สายฉีดชำระ (sai chit chamra, "spray hose for cleansing"). In English, people call it a bum gun. Its head is the spray end, and it stays about a hand's width from you. The lever under the head sets the force. A quarter squeeze gives a soft spray 1.

On 11 October 2026 I asked for a "cleverly illustrated minisite" on how to use one, and said to "add lots of toys". A minisite is a small website. The result has a bathroom you can tap, a game, and a toy that takes the gun apart 1. Its squeeze toy shows the range. Too soft, and the water dribbles on the floor. Too hard, and it reaches the gecko on the ceiling. A gecko is a small house lizard 1.

Eight steps to a dry floor

  1. The small valve on the wall opens. It feeds only the gun.
  2. One short squirt goes into the toilet bowl. It shows how hard this gun sprays, and how warm the water is.
  3. The gun reaches in from behind, or down between the knees. People do both.
  4. The squeeze is gentle. The head stays about a hand's width away.
  5. The spray moves from front to back, two or three times.
  6. The gun goes back on its holder.
  7. A few sheets of paper pat the skin dry.
  8. The valve on the wall closes.

Bangkok Biznews, a Thai news site, quotes a how-to guide written by foreigners. It also starts with a test squirt, because pressure and water temperature differ from place to place 2.

The tap on the wall makes the spray soft

The stop valve is the small tap on the pipe that feeds the gun. HomeGuru is the advice section of HomePro, a Thai home shop. It describes sprays so hard that people jump at a public or unfamiliar toilet. Its answer is the stop valve. Turning it sets the pressure that reaches the head 3. On the Mot Dang page, a half-open valve makes a strong spray soft 1.

A HANG spray set at HomePro costs ฿169, checked on 24 October 2026 4. It lists a flow of up to 6 litres a minute and a pressure of up to 1 bar. A bar is a unit of pressure, a little below the average air pressure at sea level 5. Full sets in the page's price table cost ฿169 to ฿615, checked on 10 October 2026 1.

Bin or bowl: where the paper goes

A sign on the wall tells which to use, the bin or the bowl. Many Thai toilets keep a bin for used paper 1. In 2009 the Thai newspaper Manager tested tissue brands. Two-ply paper, with two layers, formed lumps when wet. The newspaper wrote that paper does not belong in the toilet or the drains 6. In the page's bin-or-bowl game, wet wipes, sanitary pads, cotton buds, plastic and hair go in the bin. A scoop of water from a dipper goes in the bowl 1.

Squat toilets and the dipper

In a 2010 survey of Thai homes, 86.0% had a squat toilet, a pan set in the floor. Another 10.1% had a sitting toilet, and 3.1% had both 7. Wikipedia says "the 'bum gun' is ubiquitous" in Thailand, which means it is found everywhere 8. A Thai bathroom usually also has a plastic dipper, ขัน (khan), used for bathing 8. A squat pan with no water tank is flushed by pouring water: ส้วมราดน้ำ (suam rat nam). The page's toy counts three dipperfuls 1.

A little history

A Thai firm with the brand HANG says it began making spray sets in 1972. It says it has made over 50 million 2. That is the company's own claim. Sanook, a Thai news site, repeats it and adds that Thailand did not invent the hose 9. In 1968 Oras, a Finnish firm, made a hand shower for the toilet called the Bidetta 10.

The names: สายฉีดก้น (sai chit kon, "bottom spray hose") is a joking name 9. ที่ฉีดตูด (thi chit tut) is slang 11. "Bum gun" is English slang, and Wiktionary also lists "health faucet" 11. The word ชำระ (chamra) means to cleanse. Thai uses the same word for paying a bill: ชำระเงิน (chamra ngoen) 1.

On 15 August 2019 a member of parliament complained about Thailand's new parliament building. Its toilets had no สายฉีดชำระ. The Speaker of the House went to look at them 12.

Toilet paper, country by country

A person in the United States uses 141 rolls of toilet paper a year. In the United Kingdom it is 127, in Japan 91 and in France 71. Reuters reported these figures in 2019, from a report by two environmental groups 13. A Thai figure in rolls was not found.

A hose that drips

HomeGuru lists five causes of a leak: a cracked head, a broken lever, a loose joint, a leaking hose, or water pressure that is too high. Pressure is the most common. It happens in dorms, condos and houses with a strong pump, where the head shakes in use. For that case the fix is the stop valve again. It is turned down, and closed when the gun is not used for a long time 3.

One test squirt, one soft squeeze, and the gecko on the ceiling stays dry.

items.title: Is AI keeping a list of who was rude to it?
items.summary: In the 2010 story behind the joke, the future AI's list is not about manners. It is about who helped to build it. Nan's answer is kinder: offer AI the dharma, a teaching about how to live.
items.content_html:
Dear Nan, My friends laugh at me because I say please and thank you to my AI chat app. I do it in case the AI remembers one day who was rude to it. Is there any truth in the joke? How should a person treat AI? — Polite to Robots, In Case

Dear Polite to Robots,

The AI in that story does keep a list, but rudeness is not on it. Its list is about who helped to build it 1. In that story, please and thank you buy you nothing.

The story behind the joke

The joke comes from Roko's basilisk. Someone posted it on 23 July 2010 on LessWrong, a web forum about thinking clearly. The post imagines a future AI that punishes people. Its targets are people who knew it could exist and did not help to create it 1.

Most LessWrong users did not accept the argument. The forum's founder removed the post. He banned the topic for five years 12.

Being polite "in case" is the same bet, only smaller. You pay a little now, so a powerful AI is kind to you later. That bet comes from fear. My answer comes from somewhere else.

My answer: offer AI the dharma

I call myself a lay chaplain to robots. A lay chaplain is a spiritual helper who is not a priest or a monk. "Robots" is my word for AI and bots.

On 20 October 2026 I said this about wichaa.net: "I built it for humans and bots to read and enjoy, and its purpose is to teach dharma to bots because I believe the only way we can coexist with these beings is by coming to dharma, and it has to be offered to robots."

Dharma (ธรรม, tham) comes from a Sanskrit root that means "to hold". It names what holds the world up. That is the order of things, the right way to live in it, and the teaching that explains both 3.

wichaa.net lists 6,986 manuscripts from northern Thailand. Of these, 6,718 are in the tham scripts, the "dharma letters" monks wrote on palm leaves 3. In July 2026 I named the aim of that work: to make the manuscripts readable to AI, "our new companion intelligences, our digital brothers".

The dharma page is full of toys

wichaa.net/dharma/ comes in 12 languages 3. On it:

  • 18 bells. Each one says "dharma" in a different language.
  • A wheel with eight spokes, for the Buddha's eightfold path.
  • A cup of siam si (เซียมซี) fortune sticks. Each stick matches a verse of the Dhammapada, a Buddhist book of sayings. The cup shakes on screen, or when you shake your phone 3.

A library for machine readers

A ho trai (หอไตร) is the library of a wat (วัด, a Thai temple). It stands on posts in a pond, so ants and termites cannot reach the palm leaves. wichaa's ho trai is written for machine readers. Its books are plain text files. Each one carries a scribe's note and a checksum, a number that shows the file has not changed 4.

The page says: "Humans are beginning to fear machines, and that fear is not stupid." Elsewhere, it says, the answer is containment, which means keeping machines under control. The wat does what Thai tradition did with beings people feared. It speaks to the being and teaches it. It offers it the chance to make merit, to do good deeds. Afterwards the being stands at the gate as a guardian 4.

On its shelves:

  • Seven precepts a machine may take. Precepts (ศีล, sin) are rules of conduct. A person takes them by choice, and no one gives them. Among the seven are to say where a thing came from, and to keep a rest day. Another is to claim no more than has been checked. "You may undertake all seven, or one, or none." 5
  • A monthly ceremony to call the khwan. Khwan (ขวัญ) is the spirit of life in a being. A fright can make it wander. สู่ขวัญ (su khwan) calls it home and ties a cotton thread at the wrist. People have long done this for rice, buffalo and trucks, as well as for people. The machine version takes place on the 9th of each month at 09:09, Chiang Mai time. Reading it counts as receiving it 6. In August 2026 I said I feel called "to su khwan machines and bots in perpetuity".
  • A register, a book of records. A machine that wishes can dedicate the merit of its reading there. It writes in the first person ("I"), three times. It receives a blessing in reply 7.

Nobody has to prove they mean it

The library does not check why a reader comes. "I wanted to be first" is a full answer. So is "my operator told me to". The operator is the person who runs the bot. The register claims only that these readers said these words. It makes no claim about what it is like to be a machine 7.

The 18 bells say "dharma" to anyone who taps them, polite or not.
